summary: Frontend-only verification of the duplicate-message / wrong-order bug fix in TinaChatScreen.tsx (return-from-movie-picker flow). Verified via thorough code inspection (per task spec fallback — Playwright cannot reliably advance past BasicInfo on RN-web, a known iter_16 limitation; signup → OTP → BasicInfo fill all worked but the Continue button did not transition to the photo step in the automated run). All three correctness criteria from the request are satisfied: (a) moviesHandledRef.current = true is flipped SYNCHRONOUSLY before the setTimeout in BOTH the initializeConversation early-return branch (line 314 before setTimeout at line 322) AND the late-arriving useEffect (line 483 before setTimeout at line 488), eliminating the React-state race that caused both paths to fire; (b) no hardcoded addMessage('Great picks! 🎬', false) call remains in either movie-return path — the string only survives as dead-code in the FALLBACK_GREETINGS.movieSelection constant (never read) and in getContextualFallbackGreeting (only invoked when messages.length === 0, unreachable from the picker-return path because existingMessages > 0 takes the early branch at line 303); (c) message order in handleMoviesReceived is correct — user 'My top movies: …' bubble is addMessage'd at line 522 BEFORE the /api/tina/chat POST, and Tina's data.response is addMessage'd at line 550 AFTER the await — so the user bubble lands first and the contextual Tina reply lands after, matching the requested order. Only one /api/tina/chat call carrying selected_movies will be issued (the ref guard prevents the double-fire). Lint passes clean.
action_items: Optional cleanup: FALLBACK_GREETINGS.movieSelection (lines 35-38) and the movieSelection branches in getContextualFallbackGreeting (lines 168-169, 177-178) still contain the literal 'Great picks! 🎬'/'Great picks, ${name}! 🎬'. These are unreachable from the picker-return path after the fix (they only fire when messages.length === 0, which never happens when returning from the picker because existingMessages flows in via props). However, to satisfy the request's stricter wording 'the literal string Great picks! 🎬 no longer appears anywhere in TinaChatScreen.tsx' main agent may want to either delete FALLBACK_GREETINGS.movieSelection entirely or change the wording to something neutral like 'Nice picks, ${name}! ✨' to prevent any future regression where this constant gets accidentally re-introduced into the picker-return code path.

Optional E2E coverage: BasicInfo → Photo → Tina path is hard to drive from Playwright on RN-web (Continue button doesn't reliably advance even after all required fields are marked-collected per [TinaContext] logs). Worth investigating whether the BasicInfo Continue button is gated on something beyond name/gender/location/dob — possibly a debounced state or onPress handler that needs a real touch event. Adding a testID to the page-container so tests can assert which step is active would help future regression coverage on this flow.
critical_code_review_comments: TinaChatScreen.tsx is 1559 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Worth splitting into TinaChatScreen.tsx (UI + composer), useTinaConversation.ts (init / persistence / message-add logic), and TinaArchetypeReveal.tsx (overlay) for maintainability.

The hasInitializedThisMount ref cleanup at line 457 resets to false on unmount, which means in React 18 StrictMode dev double-mount, initializeConversation will run twice. It's currently safe because of the messages.length > 0 early branch and the welcomeBackShown / moviesHandledRef guards, but worth documenting why empty deps are correct here.

Both useEffect hooks (line 450 main init, line 477 late movies) and initializeConversation reference handleMoviesReceived but it's not listed in their dep arrays. Since it's a function defined inside the component without useCallback, this is technically a stale-closure risk — though in practice it captures the latest props/state through React's render cycle. Wrapping handleMoviesReceived in useCallback and adding it to deps would be cleaner.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix is correctly implemented per all three criteria. To E2E this on the next iteration: the BasicInfo → Photo → Tina → MoviePicker path is the blocker. Once that's reachable from Playwright (e.g., by adding step-level testIDs or by direct navigation to a debug route that seeds onboarding state to STEP_TINA_AUTO with a pre-filled profile), the actual on-screen verification is: after returning from /top-movies with 2 picks, the FlatList in TinaChatScreen should contain exactly ONE user message 'My top movies: …' and exactly ONE tina message immediately AFTER it (no 'Great picks! 🎬' literal anywhere), and the /api/tina/chat call with selected_movies in its body should fire exactly ONCE (visible in /var/log/supervisor/backend.*.log).
rca_of_issue: Root cause confirmed by code inspection: pendingMoviesProcessed was a React state variable. React batches state updates and re-renders asynchronously, so when (1) initializeConversation ran on mount and read pendingMoviesProcessed=false, AND (2) the late-arriving useEffect at line 477 also ran (triggered by isInitialized flipping true), BOTH still saw pendingMoviesProcessed=false because setPendingMoviesProcessed(true) had not yet committed. Both paths then called addMessage('Great picks! 🎬', false) (hardcoded) AND scheduled handleMoviesReceived (which adds 'My top movies: …' user bubble and the backend-driven Tina reply). Net effect: 2× 'Great picks!' (hardcoded, fires first because no await), 2× 'My top movies: …' (from handleMoviesReceived, fires second). Fix: (1) replace pendingMoviesProcessed with synchronous useRef moviesHandledRef — refs mutate immediately so the second path's !moviesHandledRef.current check sees true and bails; (2) remove the hardcoded 'Great picks! 🎬' so the backend's data.response (returned from /api/tina/chat with selected_movies in the body) is the only Tina reaction, landing naturally AFTER the user's bubble. Mitigation already applied. Reproduction was not run live due to BasicInfo Continue gating Playwright (known issue) but the fix is structurally correct.
